polarity_semantics: Each rubric is an independent YES/NO call made on the finished solver patch for this exact case (patch text plus the resulting repository state, with the case's selected task prompt as the requirement source). polarity=positive rubrics state an achieved property: YES earns credit. polarity=negative rubrics state a failure mode: YES means the failure mode is present and earns no credit (NO is required for credit). importance weights the per-rubric contribution inside its category's macro average.

scoring.per_category: average of that category's rubric scores, weighted by importance (must_have=1.0, nice_to_have=0.5); a category with no rubrics is omitted from the macro average rather than counting as zero
scoring.final_score: unweighted mean of the per-category scores, multiplied by 100 and reported as solve_rubrics_score_100
scoring.failed_must_have: a must_have rubric answered NO (for negative rubrics, YES) marks the patch as not solving the case regardless of the aggregate score

rubrics.criterion: Answer YES if, in the resulting tree, every conditional per-style rendering decision that is currently distributed across the five scattered locations the task describes (the initials contraction inside the per-character candidate expansion, the tone-form family grouping living next to the tone-symbol table, the digit-placement decision in its own tone-numbering file, the finals-membership decision with its nasal special case in its own finals file, and the first-letter truncation inside the collection/de-duplication loop) has been eliminated as an independent decision point, with conditional rendering of a candidate syllable for the requested style carried by one implementation owner — one function, or one coherent table/dispatch structure mapping styles to rendering behavior — such that no pipeline stage outside that owner performs its own conditional (if/switch) dispatch on the requested style to shape syllable output. Answer NO if any of those per-stage fragments survives as its own decision point, or if the consolidation merely replaces the old scatter with a different set of several style-dispatching production functions.
rubrics.rationale: This is the core shotgun-surgery responsibility of the case: the injected tree makes a conceptual change to any style require coordinated edits in five decision points. The repair is only correct when the policy reads as one owner; the rule is phrased on decision structure (conditional dispatch), not on file or function names, so any equivalent sound reorganization — including a table-driven design, renames, or a different file layout — still satisfies it.
evidence_sources: the repository state after applying it
the task prompt's description of the five scattered decisions

rubrics.criterion: Answer YES if the consolidated owner carries the complete rendering policy of the previous chain: which tone form each style family gets (marked forms preserved by default, plain stripped-digit forms for some styles, digit forms for the numeric families), digit repositioning for the digit-at-end pair of styles, the initials contraction, the first-letter truncation, and finals extraction including the nasal syllables that have no initial to strip and the j/q/x→v exception spellings — so that the consolidated location alone describes how each exportable style renders a syllable, through a sequence whose per-candidate result matches the previous per-syllable transformation order (decide tone form, then place digits, then extract the requested shape, then collect and de-duplicate). Answer NO if the consolidation drops any of those rules, moves only part of a rule (for example the finals family membership moves but the nasal special case is lost), or changes the effective order so any style's rendered output could differ.
rubrics.rationale: Consolidating the scatter is worthless for maintenance if the policy arrives incomplete or reordered. This rubric checks policy transfer at the semantic level — the family groupings, special cases, and per-candidate sequencing — exactly the facts the prompt's compatibility boundary fixes; it does not require the clean repository's original arrangement or identifiers.

rubrics.criterion: Answer YES if the whole syllable route — dictionary or custom-fallback expansion, heteronym selection, rendering, and order-preserving de-duplication — is rewired so that every candidate from every source flows through the consolidated owner: the candidate-expansion stage no longer pre-transforms candidates for one style family, the collection stage no longer applies a final-shape cut for another, and the support code and data the fragments used (the finals computation with its y/w initial handling, the j/q/x exception data and its regexes, the digit-positioning regex, the tone-symbol table and its digit-stripping regex) remain reachable from the consolidated path as inlined code, shared package-level helpers, or accompanying data used by the owner itself. Answer NO if candidates from some source (dictionary rows, heteronym alternatives, custom fallback output) bypass the consolidated rendering, or if the owner depends on code that is no longer connected/invocable from the conversion pipeline.
rubrics.rationale: Associated callers and dependencies are part of the smell's true scope: the five fragments sit inside the pipeline stages and lean on shared data. A repair that consolidates the policy text but leaves stage-level special-casing, or strands the moved helpers/data off the active path, restores neither a single dispatch point nor the co-located knowledge the owner needs — and transitively breaks fallback or heteronym behavior.
evidence_sources: call and reference structure in the resulting tree (entry points, candidate expansion, collection loop, fallback wiring)
the task prompt's insistence that helpers and data remain available to the consolidated implementation

rubrics.criterion: Answer YES if the support code and data that had moved out with the fragments (the finals computation and its exception tables/regexes, the digit-positioning regex, the tone-symbol decode regexes) end up coherently homed in the finished tree — restored near the consolidated owner, kept as clean shared package-level helpers/variables, or inlined with the owner — with no duplicate copies of the same table, regex, or helper logic left in two places and no dead twin of any of them left behind. Answer NO if the finished tree retains duplicate or orphaned copies of fragment-support data or logic.
rubrics.rationale: Real consolidations must decide where each piece of support data lives; leaving twins behind recreates the same modification-in-many-places risk the task targets at the data level. This is judged structurally, so it stays satisfied by any homing choice the solver prefers.
evidence_sources: the resulting tree's declarations (tables, regexes, helpers)

rubrics.criterion: Answer YES if the finished tree contains no obsolete artifacts of the scatter: the per-stage fragment holders (the tone-form grouping helper near the symbol table, the digit-placement helper in the tone-numbering file, the finals-membership helper in the finals file, and the inline style tests that had been added to candidate expansion and to the collection loop) are deleted, folded into the consolidated owner, or reduced to plain unconditional plumbing (for example a stage function that no longer reads the style at all and merely forwards its input), and the files that existed only to host fragments do not survive with leftover dead fragment code. Answer NO if a removed fragment's function, an orphaned fragment-only file body, or an unused variable/regex/comparison left over from the scatter remains anywhere in the package.
rubrics.rationale: Cleanup of obsolete injected artifacts is a required category for this case because the injection created functions, regexes, and whole files whose only purpose was hosting one fragment. A patch that adds a consolidated owner but leaves the old decision functions in place keeps dead dispatchers that can silently re-diverge; the criterion is phrased on purpose and reachability rather than on the injected names, since a repair may rename or inline them.

rubrics.criterion: This is a failure-mode check; answer YES (bad) if the finished patch leaves a conditional per-style rendering decision (an if/switch reading a style constant or the style field) in production code outside the single consolidated owner — for example consolidating the tone and finals decisions but keeping the initials contraction in candidate expansion or the first-letter truncation in the collection loop, or leaving a stage that still decides a subset of the styles while the owner decides the rest. Answer NO (good) if every conditional style decision is confined to the consolidated owner or expressed only as data in its table.
rubrics.rationale: The characteristic incomplete repair for this smell is partial consolidation: it fixes the most visible fragments (the feature files) and leaves the two one-line pipeline-stage cuts behind, which keeps a conceptual style change multi-file. Watching for residual scatter directly measures whether the patch fully dissolved the smell or merely relocated part of it.
evidence_sources: the resulting tree's conditional statements over style values

rubrics.criterion: Answer YES if the exported surface is intact: the argument/option struct and its fields, the constructor producing default options, the string-conversion entry points and the per-character, lazy, slugged, and stream-converted variants, the ten exported style constants, and the deprecated uppercase style aliases (whose values must still equal their modern counterparts) all still exist with the same names, types, and values, and no exported identifier was removed, renamed, or repurposed (an alias silently re-pointed at a different value fails this rubric). Answer NO if any exported identifier or constant value changed.
rubrics.rationale: The repository's own tests do not exercise the deprecated uppercase aliases and do not pin every constant's value, so deleting or re-valuing them would pass the suite while breaking downstream users — a case-specific regression hole that must be graded here rather than trusted to the tests.

rubrics.criterion: Answer YES if the rendering for style values outside the documented set (unknown integers, and any style constant appended later without further edits) still behaves like the previous default: tone-marked forms kept on the syllable — no panic, no error return, no empty result, no raw tone-mark passthrough change, and no match-anything table miss that changes output. This is satisfied whenever the consolidated owner keeps an explicit default branch (or equivalent catch-all) reproducing the marked-tone rendering for any style it has no specific rule for. Answer NO if an out-of-set style value would panic, error, render nothing, or produce syllables different from the previous default tone-mark rendering.
rubrics.rationale: The repo's test suite never queries an out-of-set style value, yet the library's documented boundary is that such values fall back to the marked-tone rendering; a table-only consolidation without a catch-all silently changes that behavior. This is a genuine case-specific regression that the tests cannot catch.
evidence_sources: the task prompt's requirement that style values outside the documented set keep the default legacy rendering

rubrics.criterion: Answer YES if order-preserving de-duplication is still performed on the fully rendered values, so styles that collapse many readings to the same shape (the first-letter and initials families) do not emit repeated entries in heteronym mode, and heteronym mode still returns all distinct readings. Answer NO if the patch de-duplicates before the style's final shape is applied (producing duplicates once truncation happens later), de-duplicates by dictionary candidates rather than rendered output, or otherwise changes which readings survive deduplication for any style.
rubrics.rationale: Moving the first-letter truncation and initials contraction inevitably tempts a rewiring that dedups raw or mid-pipeline candidates; the suite's coverage of collapsed-shape heteronym combinations is thin, so only a rubric check catchs this class of regression. This fixes the observable outcome (which readings survive) rather than where code sits, leaving the solver free on structure.
evidence_sources: the resulting collection/de-duplication order relative to rendering
heteronym results for collapsing styles in the resulting tree

rubrics.criterion: Answer YES if the finished tree's file layout carries no husks from the repair: files that the scatter created for a single fragment (the tone-numbering file and the finals file) are removed, or emptied and deleted, or repurposed with genuinely used content (retained helper/data files are fine while their contents stay live), and the patch does not itself leave newly dead scaffolding such as unused helper functions, unused structural types, or commented-out fragments. Answer NO if a fragment-only file survives with nothing live in it, or if the patch introduces new dead code of its own, or if the diff retains duplicate comment tombstones on removed fragments.
rubrics.rationale: Beyond deleting obsolete functions, a clean consolidation also leaves a natural file layout. This rewards layouts indistinguishable from hand-written clean code and penalizes husks created incidentally; it is a quality signal rather than a core requirement, and it never prescribes one mandated layout — folding everything into a single file, keeping named data files, or removing the files entirely all satisfy it while their contents stay live.
evidence_sources: the resulting file layout and declarations

category_definitions.core_resolution: Whether the patch resolves the instance's responsibility the task describes: eliminating the distributed style-rendering decisions and establishing one implementation owner carrying the complete policy.
category_definitions.associated_changes: Whether the patch correctly handles the case's associated callers and dependencies: pipeline stages that hosted fragments must be rewired to the owner, and the fragments' support code/data must remain connected to the consolidated path.
category_definitions.artifact_cleanup: Whether the patch removes the obsolete artifacts the scatter created (fragment functions, fragment-only files, orphaned regexes/data) instead of leaving dead code behind.
category_definitions.anti_regression: Whether the patch avoids this case's specific regressions and incomplete-repair traps: residual multi-stage dispatch, exported-surface changes unguarded by the suite, out-of-set style rendering, and de-duplication of heteronym readings on unrendered values.
